ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.AEFiniteKernelS.statement: Let $T$ be a countable space in which singletons are measurable, and let $\kappa$ be a kernel from $T$ to $S$ that has almost everywhere finite kernel support with respect to a measure $\mu$ on $T$ (hypothesis $h\kappa$). This defines an associated kernel $h\kappa.\mathrm{mk}$ from $T$ to $S$ (the definition does not actually use the hypothesis $h\kappa$).

Let $T$ be a countable space in which singletons are measurable, and let $S$ be a space in which singletons are measurable. If the kernel $\kappa$ from $T$ to $S$ has almost everywhere finite kernel support with respect to $\mu$ (hypothesis $h\kappa$), then the kernel $h\kappa.\mathrm{mk}$ has finite kernel support.
